proof_note: PROOF FIXTURE written by the orchestrator in an isolated engine copy (template_promote_after lowered to 1) to exercise the build -> gates -> blind-selection path end to end. Not a real library decision.
idea: Several separate conditions each arrive and draw an arrow into one outcome, so the outcome reads as their joint result.
outline: the outcome card at the centre
condition cards arriving one by one around it
an arrow from each condition drawing into the outcome
an optional label naming that they combined
variation_seen: three conditions in the source; the count and wording vary by lesson

closest_existing.falls_short: a hub radiates spokes outward from a centre; here causes converge inward on an effect and arrive on their own words

content_shape: 2 to 5 contributing conditions and one outcome they produce together

future_uses.shows: a fall caused by a wet floor, no sign, and poor lighting
a lost account from slow support, a price rise and a missing feature
a late launch from unclear scope, one reviewer, and a vendor slip

targets.narration: The fall was not caused by one thing. The floor was wet, no warning sign was out, and the corridor light had failed. Together they made the slip almost certain.
targets.visual_intent: three conditions pointing into one incident

targets.narration: The client did not leave over one bad week. Support replies were slow, the renewal price went up, and the feature they asked for never shipped. All three pushed them out.
targets.visual_intent: several reasons combining into one lost account

targets.narration: It is tempting to blame the vendor for the late launch. But the scope was unclear, only one person could review, and the vendor slipped too. The delay came from all of them.
targets.visual_intent: several causes feeding one late launch, not a single culprit

decoys.narration: First the request is logged, then it is triaged by the on call engineer, then it is fixed and tested, and finally the customer is told it is resolved.
A service level objective is a target for how reliable a service should be, such as ninety nine point nine percent of requests succeeding over a month.

reason: The convergence of several conditions on one outcome recurs in any lesson about incidents, risk or root causes, and no existing template draws causes converging inward. It is a whole-beat argument, not just a part.
